question: How does a fixed 20-observation currency momentum rule compare with equal weighting, after an explicit execution lag and transaction-cost scenarios?
source: ECB euro foreign exchange reference rates; current published historical snapshot
source_calendar_rule: Retain all raw source rows and status codes; use only dates with four positive finite published quotes, exclude missing quotes by current-date availability, never fill them
source_calendar_clarification: Added before any factor values or results: the response contains four holiday dates (16 H-status records) without quotes. The fixed date window, currencies, strategy and costs are unchanged.
benchmark: Equal-weight all four currencies on exactly the same rebalance dates
tie_break: Stable ascending currency code within equal momentum values
decision_rule: Describe whether the highest-momentum group has a greater total return than the matched equal-weight benchmark at the primary cost; do not optimize parameters after viewing results
limitations: Reference rates are information observations, not executable bid/ask quotes
Reciprocals convert quoted currency per EUR to EUR per unit; no currency interest or FX carry is modeled
The input is the currently published historical snapshot, not certified historical vintages
Costs are declared illustrative scenarios, not observed broker charges
This is a retrospective, four-currency software/research example, not a new factor admission or investment recommendation
execution_revision: V2 retains twice each one-way fee rate in cash at every scheduled rebalance, applied identically to both groups and the benchmark. V1 allowed small borrowing when fees were charged after full allocation.
revision_status: Engineering correction after V1 results were observed; not a blind or new predictive hypothesis. Formula, dates, currencies, groups and costs unchanged.
